provenance: Every answer was read out of zod 4.4.3's own TypeScript source and is cited to the file and line it came from. None came from a specification this engine produced. The published package ships compiled `.js` and `.d.ts` beside the source, so the fixture root is the `src` tree: analysing both would score a document against two copies of the same declarations.
shape: The first fixture is a Python web service and the second a Python client library. This is neither: 286 files of TypeScript that serve nothing, store nothing and start nothing. It is a validation library whose whole subject is declared patterns, exported surface and an error vocabulary -- and TypeScript is the reader known to be weakest, so this is where a specification is least likely to flatter itself.
